label: Coding
summary: Nine stages: request → reviewed pull request

stages.name: Inbox
stages.title: Capture the request
stages.body: Hive creates a task folder for the request. Its files become inputs for later stages.
stages.sample: Build a scriptable screenshot CLI. Read every note, not just the first page.

stages.name: Brainstorm
stages.title: Resolve requirements
stages.body: Questions become requirements before implementation starts.
stages.sample: JSON output. Stable exit codes. Complete note results.

stages.name: Plan
stages.title: Write the implementation plan
stages.body: The plan records scope, implementation steps, and checks for the next agent.
stages.sample: Reuse the API. Build the CLI. Check pagination and error handling.

stages.name: Execute
stages.title: Implement in a worktree
stages.body: The builder receives the plan and works on the task branch.
stages.sample: Plan → implementation → commit. The task keeps its prior documents.

stages.name: Open PR
stages.title: Open a draft pull request
stages.body: The change and its context are linked in a draft pull request.
stages.sample: A draft PR is a review surface, not a claim that the work is finished.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Review the implementation
stages.body: In the recorded Screenote task, review caught notes disappearing after screenshot 100.
stages.sample: Finding: fetch every page, not just the first 100 screenshots.

stages.name: Artifacts
stages.title: Collect checks and evidence
stages.body: Save check results and supporting artifacts for the final handoff.
stages.sample: Targeted API and Go checks passed. The full Rails suite was blocked by missing libvips.

stages.name: Finalize
stages.title: Prepare the handoff
stages.body: The PR, review history, and handoff notes stay together.
stages.sample: Reviewed changes and their evidence. Ready for a human to inspect.

stages.name: Done
stages.title: Archive the completed task
stages.body: The task is archived with its artifacts. Completion does not promise an automatic merge.
stages.sample: The recorded Screenote PR was later merged. Inspect the historical result below.

route.title: Fix the review findings
route.body: The same task returns to execution with its review findings, requirements, and plan.
route.sample: Fix: fetch all pages and surface real API errors.

route.title: Recheck the fix
route.body: The change returns to review. Bounded review can still stop for human intervention.
route.sample: The pagination fix is rechecked before the workflow moves on.

label: Writing
summary: Seven stages: evidence → draft → editorial revisions → article
completion: This sample reaches editorial consensus. The real workflow can instead return a NOT PUBLISHABLE notice for unsupported claims or the five-round limit.

stages.name: Inbox
stages.title: Set the brief
stages.body: Specify the reader, angle, voice, freshness date, and sources the article must cover.
stages.sample: For small teams: explain what a successful backup does—and does not—prove about recovery.

stages.name: Repo research
stages.title: Check the team’s own evidence
stages.body: Inspect relevant repository files. Keep path-and-line references, candidate claims, and gaps that need external verification.
stages.sample: The backup script records successful uploads. The runbook has no timed restore result.

stages.name: Web research
stages.title: Collect external sources
stages.body: Open the sources behind external claims. Record URLs, authors, dates, credibility limits, and unresolved questions.
stages.sample: Use database recovery documentation. A storage provider’s durability claim is not evidence of the team’s restore time.

stages.name: Research
stages.title: Build a source-to-claim ledger
stages.body: Synthesize the two research files into an outline and a claim map: supported, qualified, disputed, or unsupported.
stages.sample: Supported: backups complete. Unsupported: recovery takes under an hour. Omit that promise; explain what a restore test must measure.

stages.name: Draft
stages.title: Write from the evidence
stages.body: Use brief.md and research.md to write a complete draft. Material factual claims must trace back to the source ledger.
stages.sample: Explain the backup process, its limits, and how a restore drill tests the assumptions.

stages.name: Editorial
stages.title: Two editors challenge the draft
stages.body: A grounding editor checks claim support. An adversarial editor checks the argument and usefulness. The council can revise and recheck for up to five rounds.
stages.sample: Grounding: remove the unsupported “one-hour recovery” promise. Adversarial: put the restore-test checklist before the conclusion.

stages.name: Deliver
stages.title: Deliver the article and its checks
stages.body: Write article.md and verification.md with claim support, revision deltas, editorial rounds, and the terminal reason. Delivery does not publish the article.
stages.sample: Sample outcome: ready. Both editors agree; the recovery claim is qualified. Unsupported work or an exhausted round limit is marked NOT PUBLISHABLE.

route.title: Revise within the editorial council
route.body: The council’s reviser replaces draft.md using both editor reports and triage. Research and earlier review decisions stay with the task.
route.sample: Remove the untested recovery promise. Move the restore checklist earlier. Record both changes in the revision note.

route.title: Both editors check the revision
route.body: The next round checks the new draft against the same evidence. This sample reaches consensus in round two; the package allows at most five rounds.
route.sample: Grounding editor: ready. Adversarial editor: ready. The supported claims and material revisions are recorded.

label: Architecture
task: A backup design the team can test
summary: Eight stages: repository + web evidence → reviewed architecture
result: architecture.md with owner decisions and reviewer findings
completion: The design preserves the untested restore-time assumption and the owner’s cost decision. Completion does not mean every finding is resolved or the design is approved.

stages.name: Inbox
stages.title: Frame the architecture question
stages.body: Record the desired outcome, settled constraints, non-goals, and decisions that still need the owner.
stages.sample: Design off-site backups for the team’s PostgreSQL app. Aim for a one-hour restore; keep the current hosting.

stages.name: Repo research
stages.title: Find the constraints in the repository
stages.body: Read relevant code, configuration, tests, and runbooks. Cite path-and-line evidence and separate observed behavior from inference.
stages.sample: Nightly dumps and off-site uploads exist. A restore command exists, but there is no timed restore evidence.

stages.name: Web research
stages.title: Check the external contracts
stages.body: Open primary sources for recovery behavior, storage limits, and security guidance. Keep dates, URLs, applicability limits, and unanswered questions.
stages.sample: Database guidance supports restore testing. Storage durability describes retained objects—not how quickly this app can recover.

stages.name: Research
stages.title: Separate facts, assumptions, and choices
stages.body: Read both evidence collections. Synthesize only what changes the decision; do not silently turn gaps into facts.
stages.sample: Known: daily off-site copies. Untested: one-hour recovery. Owner decision: acceptable data loss and storage cost.

stages.name: Draft
stages.title: Draft the smallest workable design
stages.body: Describe components, data flow, failure paths, alternatives, rollout, rollback, and tests. Tie material decisions to the saved evidence.
stages.sample: Keep off-site backups; add restore drills and failure alerts. Define retention, encryption, and a recovery runbook.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Challenge constraints and operations
stages.body: Two reviewers examine missing evidence, tradeoffs, interfaces, and operational risks. The council can revise and recheck within a two-round limit.
stages.sample: Constraints: recovery time is still an assumption. Operations: the restore drill must test loss of the primary credentials.

stages.name: Architecture
stages.title: Deliver the design with open decisions
stages.body: Write the final architecture with traceable evidence, a test plan, owner decisions, and resolved, deferred, or rejected reviewer findings.
stages.sample: Add a timed recovery drill using separate credentials. Keep the one-hour target unverified until measured; leave the cost choice for the owner.

stages.name: Done
stages.title: Keep the completed architecture
stages.body: Done is inert: no additional agent runs. The final design and its research and review trail remain together.
stages.sample: architecture.md is ready for implementation planning. Unsettled owner choices and deferred findings remain explicit.

route.title: Revise the design inside the council
route.body: The council’s reviser replaces draft.md from the saved findings. Resolve each blocker or record an evidence-backed disagreement; keep unresolved owner choices visible.
route.sample: Add a timed restore drill with separately recoverable credentials. Change “meets one hour” to an acceptance target that still needs measurement.

route.title: Recheck the load-bearing changes
route.body: Both reviewers assess the revised draft in round two. The package can finish at its round limit without consensus; unresolved findings must survive into architecture.md.
route.sample: Credential recovery is addressed. Restore-time validation remains deferred to the drill; the final design must say so.
